meta.title: First Half Marathon
meta.subtitle: Go from 5 km to 21 km without getting hurt
meta.description: A 12 week plan for a first half marathon. Nothing to do with technology: the format works for any goal.
meta.tagline:
One block at a time.
Consistency beats intensity.
meta.sidebarNote:
A generic example plan.
Check with a professional if you have any pain or condition.

labels.success: How to tell it went well
labels.doneHint: Mark this after completing the key workout, even if slower than planned.
labels.legendHint: Click a block to see the key workout and how to judge the result.

phases.title: Base
phases.summary: Build the habit and settle into 5 to 8 km comfortably.

phases.title: Volume
phases.summary: Grow the long run gradually and learn to eat during a run.

phases.title: Race
phases.summary: Cut the load, rest and arrive in good shape.

nodes.title: Starting point
nodes.summary: Measure where you are and choose shoes, times and fixed days.
nodes.challenge: Run 5 km at your own pace and write down the time and how you felt.
nodes.success: You have the three weekly days reserved in your calendar.

nodes.title: Easy runs
nodes.summary: Run slowly, at a pace where you can still hold a conversation.
nodes.challenge: Three workouts of 30 to 40 minutes at an easy pace.
nodes.success: You finish every workout feeling you could keep going.

nodes.title: Strength and mobility
nodes.summary: Strengthen legs and core to reduce the risk of injury.
nodes.challenge: Two 20 minute sessions per week throughout the block.
nodes.success: You do the sequence without breaks and without pain.

nodes.title: Progressive long run
nodes.summary: One longer run per week, growing from 10 to 16 km.
nodes.challenge: Run 16 km at an easy pace at the end of the block.
nodes.success: You finish with enough energy to walk home without pain.

nodes.title: Tempo runs
nodes.summary: One harder workout per week, to learn the race pace.
nodes.challenge: Run 5 km holding the pace you plan to use in the race.
nodes.success: The last kilometers are as even as the first ones.

nodes.title: Eating during the run
nodes.summary: Test gels, drinks and timing on long runs, never only on race day.
nodes.challenge: Do a long run using exactly what you will carry in the race.
nodes.success: No stomach trouble and no drop in energy.

nodes.title: Hill workout
nodes.summary: Build leg strength with repeats on short hills.

nodes.title: Cutting the load
nodes.summary: Lower the volume and keep a little intensity so you arrive rested.
nodes.challenge: One 10 km workout at race pace in week 10.
nodes.success: You feel with more energy, not less.

nodes.title: Race day
nodes.summary: Arrive early, warm up a little and start slower than seems necessary.
nodes.success: You cross the finish line and already know what the next goal is.

nodes.title: Recovery week
nodes.summary: Return gradually, with walks and easy workouts.
